title: Simplify /balances to pairwise balances (drop debt-minimization)
declaredInterface: GET /balances -> {net: {person: amount}, pairwise: [{from, to, amount}]} (replaces the greedy-minimized `settlements` list with direct pairwise net balances between each pair of people)
assumptions: User asked to replace the transaction-minimizing settle-up algorithm with straightforward pairwise balances (net debt between each pair of people who've shared an expense together), dropping simplifyDebts.

completion.whatWasBuilt: Replaced the greedy transaction-minimizing settle-up algorithm in GET /balances with straightforward pairwise balances: for each pair of people who've shared an expense, the net amount one owes the other, computed directly from expense history rather than routed through a third person.

decisions.why: User explicitly asked for simple pairwise balances instead of transaction minimization
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Keeping both and exposing two fields; rejected as unnecessary complexity the user didn't ask for

decisions.decision: GET /balances response field renamed from `settlements` to `pairwise`
decisions.why: Name should reflect what it now represents (direct pairwise debts, not a minimized settle-up plan)
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Keeping the `settlements` name for backward compatibility - not warranted, no external consumers yet

decisions.why: Still useful summary info and wasn't part of what the user asked to change

filesChanged.purpose: computeNetBalances unchanged; simplifyDebts removed and replaced with computePairwiseBalances (direct per-pair net debt, no third-party routing)
GET /balances now returns {net, pairwise} instead of {net, settlements}
Replaced simplifyDebts tests with pairwise tests, including a case proving debt is never routed through a third person
Documented the new pairwise response shape

completion.knownLimitations: Pairwise balances can produce more visible line items than a minimized settle-up plan would (e.g. A owes B and B owes C stay separate rather than collapsing) - that's the intended behavior per this change.
completion.nextSteps: None pending from this change; still waiting on frontend work.
